source.book: Original kid paraphrases. Book 1 is Genesis 1-2. Book 2 is Genesis 6-9. Book 3 is Exodus 1:22 and 2:1-10. Book 4 is Jonah 1-3. Book 5 is 1 Samuel 17. Not a copyrighted Bible translation.
source.copyrightNote: Short original Tigrinya lines and English glosses for young children. Do not paste a published translation.
source.shape: Creation uses a weekday refrain. Sunday is the first day. Friday is the sixth day, when the people are made. Saturday is the seventh-day rest. Tuesday, the third day, has two pages: land and sea, then grass and trees. Noah is one connected paraphrase of Genesis 6-9: evil on the earth, Noah righteous and obedient, the ark, the family, the animals two by two, the shut door and the rain, the water, the raven, the dove, then dry land, then the rainbow promise. Moses is one connected paraphrase of the basket story: Pharaoh's order, the mother keeping the baby, the papyrus basket in the reeds, the sister watching, the princess finding him, her pity, the sister bringing the mother as nurse, the nursing, the name Moses, and God keeping the baby safe. Jonah is one connected paraphrase of Jonah 1-3: God commands Jonah to go to Nineveh, Jonah runs and boards a ship to Tarshish, a storm, afraid sailors, Jonah says to throw him into the sea, the storm stops, a big fish swallows him, he prays for three days, the fish sets him on dry land, God commands him again and this time he obeys, Nineveh listens and turns, and God mercifully forgives them. David is one connected paraphrase of 1 Samuel 17: young David tends his father's sheep and saves them from a lion or a bear, his father sends him with food to his brothers in the army, Goliath shouts, the soldiers are afraid, David tells Saul that God will help him, Saul's armor is too big, David takes his sling and five smooth stones from the stream, he faces Goliath, one stone and Goliath falls with no gore, the people rejoice, and little David is brave because he trusted God.
source.orthographyNote: God's name is እግዚኣብሄር with ሄ, the spelling in ትመ15 (YouVersion Bible 2998). Noah is ኖህ. Evil is ክፋእ. Righteous is ፃድቕ, as in Genesis 6:9. The ark is መርከብ. God commanded ኣዘዞ. Shut is ዓፀዎ. They went out ወፁ. The raven is ኳዅ, sent ሰደዶ. The dove is ርግቢ, sent ሰደዳ, returned ተመለሰት, holding ቘፅሊ ኣውሊዕ. Dry land is ንቑጽ. The bow is ቀስቲ. The promise is ኪዳን, as in Genesis 9 ኪዳነይ. Rain keeps the pack word ዝናብ; ትመ15 writes ዝናም. Trees in Creation follow ኣእዋም. Grass keeps ሳዕሪ. Creation's good stays ጽቡቕ; ትመ15 writes ፅቡቕ. Moses keeps ሙሴ, the river ሩባ, the reeds ሰልሰላ, and the sister ሓፍቱ. Yosief's line pass spells Pharaoh ፈርኦን, the basket ሳጹን, and the nurse ሞግዚት. Pharaoh's order is ኣዘዘ. Kid lines use ኣ, never አ. She saw the basket is ረኣየቶ. The name line is ስለዝተረኽበ, ሴመቶ. Jonah keeps ትመ15 ዮናስ, ነነዌ, ተርሴስ, መርከብ, መርከበኛታት, ማዕበል, and ዓሳ. The command is ኣዘዞ, as in ነቲ ዓሳ ኣዘዞ. The storm stops as ማዕበል ደው በለ. Dry land stays the everyday ንቑጽ ምድሪ; ትመ15 writes ንቑፅ ምድሪ. Prayer is the everyday ጸለየ. Mercy is ምሕረት and ይቕረ በሎም. Yosief's Jonah pass spells the storm ዓቢይ, they saw it ርእዮም, and throw me ደርቡይኒ. The fish stays ዓባይ ዓሳ. David keeps ትመ15 1 Samuel 17: ዳዊት, ጐልያድ (ጐ as ትመ15 writes the name), ሳኦል, ፍልስጥኤማውያን, and እስራኤል. The sling is ወንጭፍ, slung is ወንጨፈ. Five smooth stones are ሓሙሽተ ልሙፃት ኣእማን from the ሩባ. One stone is ሓንቲ እምኒ, feminine with እምኒ. The bear is ድቢ, as in 1 Samuel 17:34. Armor is ክዳን; Saul clothes him ኸደኖ. He fell is the everyday ወደቐ. The giant is ዓቢይ, masculine, as ማዕበል is ዓቢይ. No beheading and no blood.
source.unlockNote: In the Beginning is the free taste. It opens before any School Path unit is finished. Noah's Ark is not free: it uses the ordinary band-1 progress gate (learned the 8th family), the same gate the Amharic band-1 library uses. Baby Moses uses the next band, band 2 (learned the 16th family). On the Tigrinya pack that family is nye, the last family of School Path chapter 2. Jonah uses the next band after Moses, band 3 (learned the 24th family). On the Tigrinya pack that family is ye. David and Goliath uses the next band after Jonah, band 4, the same gate the Amharic band-4 library uses: the last family. On the Tigrinya pack that family is pe. It does not change the Creation unlock, the Noah unlock, the Moses unlock, the Jonah unlock, the School Path unlocks, or the Amharic tracks.
source.artNote: God is not drawn. Each painting shows the thing that page names. Creation and Noah stay in highland light. Moses is the Nile: papyrus reeds, the river, and a mudbrick palace for Pharaoh and his daughter. People have deep brown skin and wear sand, linen, or sage. No bright red, no modern dress, no headscarf. The order stays gentle: no harm is shown. Jonah is the sea and an ancient city: a wooden ship, a gentle big fish, dry land, and Nineveh's walls. God is only empty sky and soft light. The fish is calm, not a monster. The king, when shown, is clearly royal and dressed apart from the people. David is a highland valley: the same young shepherd on every page, fat-tailed sheep, a lion and a bear that do not attack, an army camp, King Saul in a richer earth robe and a simple circlet, Goliath tall and bronze-armored but calm, a stream with five smooth stones, one stone and a fall with no blood and no wound. God is empty sky only.

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ሰንበት ብርሃን ፈጠረ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet senbet brhan fetere.
pages.meaningEn: On Sunday God made the light.
pages.pictureHint: Highland dawn, gold light breaking over dry ridges, no sun disk yet, no people

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ሰኑይ ሰማይ ፈጠረ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet senuy semay fetere.
pages.meaningEn: On Monday God made the sky.
pages.pictureHint: A vast highland blue sky, a few high clouds, only a thin escarpment

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ሰሉስ ምድሪን ባሕሪን ፈጠረ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet selus midrin bahrin fetere.
pages.meaningEn: On Tuesday God made the land and the sea.
pages.pictureHint: Ochre highland hills meeting a clear turquoise Red Sea, no people, no boats

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ሰሉስ ሳዕሪን ኣእዋምን ፈጠረ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet selus sarin aawamin fetere.
pages.meaningEn: On Tuesday God made the grass and the trees.
pages.pictureHint: Short highland grass, a baobab and acacias, plants only

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ረቡዕ ጸሓይን ወርሒን ፈጠረ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet rebu tsehayin werhin fetere.
pages.meaningEn: On Wednesday God made the sun and the moon.
pages.pictureHint: Highland sky with a large warm sun and a large silver moon

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ሓሙስ ኣዕዋፍን ዓሳን ፈጠረ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet hamus aawafin asan fetere.
pages.meaningEn: On Thursday God made the birds and the fish.
pages.pictureHint: Horn birds in a highland sky and large friendly fish in clear sea water

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ዓርቢ ሰብኣይን ሰበይቲን ፈጠረ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet arbi sebayin sebeytin fetere.
pages.meaningEn: On Friday God made a man and a woman.
pages.pictureHint: A man and a woman with deep brown skin, modest long cotton clothes, standing by a baobab

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብዕለት ቀዳም ዓረፈ። ኩሉ ጽቡቕ።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-ilet qedam arefe. Kullu tsbuq.
pages.meaningEn: On Saturday God rested. Everything was good.
pages.pictureHint: Quiet highland evening, the same two people resting under a baobab, a goat lying down, sea still

question.meaningEn: What did God make on Friday?

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ሰብ ኣብ ምድሪ ክፋእ ከም ዝገብር ረኣየ።
pages.latin: Igziabher seb ab mdri kfa' kem zigebr re'aye.
pages.meaningEn: God saw that people were doing evil on the earth.
pages.pictureHint: A few adults with deep brown skin in sand and sage cloth, turned away from each other, unkind but not violent, no Noah, no God

pages.geez: ኖህ ግና ፃድቕ ሰብ ነበረ። ንእግዚኣብሄር ድማ ይስምዖ ነበረ።
pages.latin: Noh gna tsadq seb nebere. Ni-Igziabher dma yism'o nebere.
pages.meaningEn: But Noah was a righteous man. He obeyed God.
pages.pictureHint: Noah alone, deep brown skin, sand linen tunic, calm, looking toward an empty sky, no divine figure

pages.geez: ማይ ብዙሕ ስለ ዝመጽእ፡ እግዚኣብሄር ንኖህ ዓባይ መርከብ ክሰርሕ ኣዘዞ።
pages.latin: May bzux sle zimetsi', Igziabher ni-Noh abay merkeb kiserh azzezo.
pages.meaningEn: Because a lot of water was coming, God commanded Noah to build a big ark.
pages.pictureHint: Noah beside timber and the frame of a big wooden ark, a soft cloud on the horizon, empty sky, no God

pages.geez: ኖህን ሰበይቱን ደቁን ነታ መርከብ ሰርሑ።
pages.latin: Nohn sebeytun dequn neta merkeb serhu.
pages.meaningEn: Noah, his wife, and his children built the ark.
pages.pictureHint: Noah, his wife, and two children building a wooden ark, sand linen and sage clothes, braided hair, no red, no animals

pages.geez: ድሕሪኡ ኖህን ሰበይቱን ደቁን ናብታ መርከብ ኣተዉ።
pages.latin: Dhr'u Nohn sebeytun dequn nabta merkeb atewu.
pages.meaningEn: After that, Noah, his wife, and his children went into the ark.
pages.pictureHint: Noah, his wife, and two children walking into the open door of the wooden ark, no animals

pages.geez: እንስሳታት ከኣ ክልተ ክልተ ምስኦም ኣተዉ።
pages.latin: Insisatat ke'a kilte kilte msom atewu.
pages.meaningEn: And the animals went in with them, two by two.
pages.pictureHint: Clear pairs of lions, giraffes, elephants, and birds walking into the ark, calm, family small in the doorway

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ናይታ መርከብ ማዕጾ ዓፀዎ። ሽዑ ዝናብ መጸ።
pages.latin: Igziabher nayta merkeb ma'tso 'ats'o. Shyu znab metse.
pages.meaningEn: God shut the door of the ark. Then the rain came.
pages.pictureHint: The ark door shut, gentle rain beginning, no hand, no face, no people in distress

pages.geez: ማይ ነታ ምድሪ ሸፈነ። እታ መርከብ ግና ኣብ ልዕሊኡ ሰላም ነበረት።
pages.latin: May neta mdri shefene. Ita merkeb gna ab l'liu selam neberet.
pages.meaningEn: Water covered the land. But the ark was safe on the water.
pages.pictureHint: Calm water over highland hills, the wooden ark floating safely, no storm, no people

pages.geez: ዝናብ ደው ምስ በለ፡ ኖህ ቅድም ንኳዅ ሰደዶ። ኳዅ ግና ኣይተመለሰን።
pages.latin: Znab dew ms bele, Noh qdm n-kwakh sededo. Kwakh gna aytemelesen.
pages.meaningEn: When the rain stopped, Noah first sent the raven. But the raven did not come back.
pages.pictureHint: Noah at the ark window watching a black raven fly away over calm water, no dove, no olive leaf, no rainbow

pages.geez: ድሕሪኡ ንርግቢ ሰደዳ። ርግቢ ቘፅሊ ኣውሊዕ ሒዛ ናብ ኖህ ተመለሰት።
pages.latin: Dhr'u n-rgbi sededa. Rgbi qotsli awli' hiza nab Noh temeleset.
pages.meaningEn: Then he sent the dove. The dove came back to Noah holding an olive leaf.
pages.pictureHint: Clear sky, Noah at the ark window, one dove arriving with a clear olive sprig, no rainbow

pages.geez: ኖህን ስድራቤቱን ናብ ንቑጽ ምድሪ ወፁ።
pages.latin: Nohn sdrabetun nab nquts mdri wetsu.
pages.meaningEn: Noah and his family went out onto dry land.
pages.pictureHint: Noah, his wife, and two children stepping onto dry ochre land from the ark, clear sky, no rainbow

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ቀስቲ ኣብ ሰማይ ኣንበረ። እዚ ኪዳን እዩ።
pages.latin: Igziabher qesti ab semay anbere. Izi kidan iyu.
pages.meaningEn: God set a rainbow in the sky. This is his promise.
pages.pictureHint: The same family on dry land, a soft rainbow across the sky, the ark on the shore, no divine figure

question.meaningEn: What did God set in the sky?

pages.geez: ፈርኦን ንህዝቡ ነቶም ንእሽቶ ኣወዳት ክጎድእዎም ኣዘዘ።
pages.latin: Fer'on n-hzbu netom n'ishto awedat kgod'wom azzeze.
pages.meaningEn: Pharaoh commanded his people to harm the little boys.
pages.pictureHint: Pharaoh in a mudbrick Egyptian hall with lotus columns, deep brown skin, sand linen, one hand raised in an order, two officials in sage and undyed linen looking down, worried, no children, no violence, no God

pages.geez: እታ ኣደ ግና ንህፃና ሰለስተ ወርሒ ኣብ ቤት ዓቒባቶ።
pages.latin: Ita ade gna n-htsana seleste werhi ab bet 'aqibato.
pages.meaningEn: But the mother kept her baby safe at home for three months.
pages.pictureHint: A mother with deep brown skin in undyed linen holding a tiny baby close inside a simple mudbrick room, a woven mat, warm quiet light, no basket, no river, no palace

pages.geez: ምሕብኡ ምስ ሰኣነት፡ ብሻምብቆ ሳጹን ሰርሐት።
pages.latin: Mhba'u ms se'anet, b-shambqo sagtsun serhet.
pages.meaningEn: When she could no longer hide him, she made a papyrus basket.
pages.pictureHint: The same mother weaving a small tight papyrus basket, cut papyrus stalks beside her, the baby wrapped nearby but not in the basket yet, earth linen, no river, no palace

pages.geez: ነቲ ህፃን ኣብቲ ሳጹን ኣእትያ፡ ኣብ ሰልሰላ ሩባ ኣንበረቶ።
pages.latin: Neti htsan abti sagtsun a'tiya, ab selsela ruba anbereto.
pages.meaningEn: She put the baby in the basket and set it among the reeds of the river.
pages.pictureHint: The mother kneeling at a calm Nile edge, setting a small papyrus basket with the baby among tall green papyrus reeds, deep brown skin, sand linen, no sister, no princess

pages.geez: ሓፍቱ ርሕቕ ኢላ ደው በለት። ነቲ ሳጹን ውን ትርኢ ነበረት።
pages.latin: Haftu rhq ila dew belet. Neti sagtsun wn tri neberet.
pages.meaningEn: His sister stood far away. She was watching the basket too.
pages.pictureHint: A young girl with deep brown skin and braided hair, sage linen, standing still at a distance among papyrus, watching a small basket in the reeds, no princess, no mother in the foreground

pages.geez: ጓል ፈርኦን ናብ ሩባ ወረደት። ነቲ ሳጹን ኣብ ሰልሰላ ረኣየቶ።
pages.latin: Gwal Fer'on nab ruba weredet. Neti sagtsun ab selsela re'ayeto.
pages.meaningEn: Pharaoh's daughter went down to the river. She saw the basket in the reeds.
pages.pictureHint: Pharaoh's daughter at the Nile among papyrus, sand linen sheath and a muted earth collar, braided hair with no headscarf, looking at a closed papyrus basket in the reeds, no crying baby visible, no sister

pages.geez: እቲ ህፃን ምስ በኸየ፡ ጓል ፈርኦን ራህርሀትሉ።
pages.latin: Iti htsan ms bekheye, gwal Fer'on raherhatlu.
pages.meaningEn: When the baby cried, Pharaoh's daughter felt pity for him.
pages.pictureHint: The papyrus basket open among reeds, a crying baby, Pharaoh's daughter leaning close with a tender worried face, sand linen, no sister, no mother

pages.geez: ሓፍቱ ሞግዚት ክረኽበልኪ በለታ።
pages.latin: Haftu mogzit krehkebelki belet.
pages.meaningEn: His sister told her, "I will find a nurse for you."
pages.pictureHint: The young sister speaking to Pharaoh's daughter beside the basket in the reeds, the sister's hand open in an offer, both in linen and sage, no mother yet

pages.geez: እታ ሞግዚት ናይቲ ህፃን ኣደ እያ። ሓፍቱ ናብ ጓል ፈርኦን ወሰደታ።
pages.latin: Ita mogzit nayti htsan ade iya. Haftu nab gwal Fer'on wesedetta.
pages.meaningEn: The nurse was the baby's mother. His sister took her to Pharaoh's daughter.
pages.pictureHint: The sister leading the mother toward the princess and the basket at the river, three people, deep brown skin, linen and sage, the mother clearly the one being brought

pages.geez: እታ ኣደ ነቲ ህፃን ኣጥበወቶ። እቲ ህፃን ድማ ዓብየ።
pages.latin: Ita ade neti htsan atbeweto. Iti htsan dma abye.
pages.meaningEn: The mother nursed the baby. And the baby grew.
pages.pictureHint: The mother nursing a content baby in a quiet shaded reed shelter, sand linen, peaceful, no palace crowd, no God

pages.geez: ጓል ፈርኦን ካብ ማይ ስለዝተረኽበ ሙሴ ኢላ ሴመቶ።
pages.latin: Gwal Fer'on kab may slezterekhbe Muse ila semeto.
pages.meaningEn: Because he was found in the water, Pharaoh's daughter named him Moses.
pages.pictureHint: Pharaoh's daughter holding a small healthy child at the river's edge, calm water and papyrus behind them, sand linen, a naming moment, no God, no text

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ነቲ ህፃን ሙሴ ሓለዎ። ሰላም ረኸበ።
pages.latin: Igziabher neti htsan Muse halewo. Selam rekhebe.
pages.meaningEn: God watched over baby Moses. He was safe.
pages.pictureHint: The baby safe and asleep in his mother's arms among quiet papyrus at dawn, soft empty sky, no person in the clouds, no hand, no face of God, warm and still

question.geez: እታ ኣደ ነቲ ህፃን ኣበይ ኣንበረቶ?
question.meaningEn: Where did the mother set the baby?

refrain.meaningEn: Listen to God the first time.

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ንዮናስ ናብ ነነዌ ክኸይድ ኣዘዞ።
pages.latin: Igziabher ni-Yonas nab Ninewe kikeyd azzezo.
pages.meaningEn: God commanded Jonah to go to Nineveh.
pages.pictureHint: Jonah, a Horn-of-Africa man with deep brown skin, short hair, and a short beard, in an undyed sand-linen tunic, standing on a dusty road and listening toward a huge ancient walled city on the horizon. Soft gold light in an empty sky. No figure, face, or hand in the sky. No text.

pages.geez: ዮናስ ግና ሃደመ። ናብ ተርሴስ መርከብ ኣተወ።
pages.latin: Yonas gna hademe. Nab Terses merkeb atewe.
pages.meaningEn: But Jonah ran away. He boarded a ship to Tarshish.
pages.pictureHint: The same Jonah walking up a wooden gangplank onto an ancient single-sail trading ship at a harbor, looking away from the distant city. Sailors in sage and sand linen. No modern boat, no God, no text.

pages.geez: እታ መርከብ ኣብ ባሕሪ ከላ፡ ዓቢይ ማዕበል መጸ።
pages.latin: Ita merkeb ab bahri kela, abiy ma'ibel metse.
pages.meaningEn: While the ship was on the sea, a big storm came.
pages.pictureHint: The same ancient wooden ship on a high sea, large grey-green waves and dark clouds, the ship still upright. The storm is the subject. No drowning, no God, no text.

pages.geez: እቶም መርከበኛታት ነቲ ማዕበል ርእዮም ፈርሑ።
pages.latin: Itom merkebenyatat neti ma'ibel r'iyom ferhu.
pages.meaningEn: The sailors saw the storm and were afraid.
pages.pictureHint: Three sailors on the ancient deck, deep brown skin, sand and sage tunics, no hats or headscarves, faces clearly afraid as they look at big waves. No Jonah in front, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ዮናስ ንመርከበኛታት፡ እዚ ማዕበል ብሰንከይ ኢዩ፡ ናብዚ ባሕሪ ደርቡይኒ በሎም።
pages.latin: Yonas ni-merkebenyatat, izi ma'ibel b-senkey iyu, nabzi bahri derbuyni belom.
pages.meaningEn: This storm is because of me. Throw me in.
pages.pictureHint: Jonah standing on an ancient sailing ship speaking to the sailors, one hand toward the sea, mouth open, the sailors listening. Earth linen, deep brown skin. No one is in the water yet. No God, no text.

pages.geez: እቶም መርከበኛታት ንዮናስ ናብ ባሕሪ ደርበይዎ። ማዕበል ደው በለ።
pages.latin: Itom merkebenyatat ni-Yonas nab bahri derbeywo. Ma'ibel dew bele.
pages.meaningEn: The sailors threw Jonah into the sea. The storm stopped.
pages.pictureHint: Sailors on an ancient wooden sailing ship with one mast and a sail, lowering Jonah over the side into the sea. The waves are calming and the sky is clearing. Not an ark, not a houseboat. Deep brown skin, earth linen, no headscarves, no bright red. No fish yet, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ሽዑ ዓባይ ዓሳ ንዮናስ ውሕጦ።
pages.latin: Shyu abay asa ni-Yonas wuhito.
pages.meaningEn: Then a big fish swallowed Jonah.
pages.pictureHint: A very large gentle fish with soft eyes and no sharp teeth, rounded and calm, taking Jonah gently into the water beside the ship. Kid-friendly, not a monster. Deep brown skin on Jonah, sand tunic. No God, no text.

pages.geez: ዮናስ ኣብ ከብዲ እቲ ዓሳ ሰለስተ መዓልቲ ጸለየ።
pages.latin: Yonas ab kebdi iti asa seleste me'alti tseleye.
pages.meaningEn: Jonah prayed in the belly of the fish for three days.
pages.pictureHint: Inside the fish as a soft warm amber cave, not scary and not gory. Jonah kneeling peacefully with hands together in prayer, sand linen, deep brown skin, calm face. No God figure, no text.

pages.geez: እቲ ዓሳ ንዮናስ ኣብ ንቑጽ ምድሪ ኣንበሮ።
pages.latin: Iti asa ni-Yonas ab nquts mdri anbero.
pages.meaningEn: The fish set Jonah on dry land.
pages.pictureHint: The same gentle blue-grey fish from the swallowing page, white belly, soft eye, no teeth, releasing Jonah onto a dry ochre shore. Same fish, not a different colorful one. Dry land, sparse grass, sea behind. No city, no God, no text.

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ዳግማይ ኣዘዞ። ዮናስ ሰሚዑ ናብ ነነዌ ከደ።
pages.latin: Igziabher dagmay azzezo. Yonas sem'u nab Ninewe kede.
pages.meaningEn: God commanded him again. Jonah listened and went to Nineveh.
pages.pictureHint: Jonah walking toward the huge ancient city gate of Nineveh, determined and calm, sand linen, deep brown skin. Soft empty sky light, no figure in the sky. The city is large, mudbrick, ancient. No text.

pages.geez: ሰብ ነነዌ ንእግዚኣብሄር ሰምዑ። ካብ ክፉእ መንገዶም ተመለሱ።
pages.latin: Seb Ninewe ni-Igziabher sem'u. Kab kfu' mengedom temelesu.
pages.meaningEn: The people of Nineveh listened to God. They turned from their bad way.
pages.pictureHint: Jonah standing before a small crowd of Horn-of-Africa people in plain earth linen, heads bowed, listening. One king stands apart in a longer earth-gold robe and a simple circlet, clearly royal, not in bright red, no headscarf. Ancient city wall behind them. No God, no text.

pages.geez: እግዚኣብሄር ብምሕረት ንሰብ ነነዌ ይቕረ በሎም።
pages.latin: Igziabher b-mhret ni-seb Ninewe yiqre belom.
pages.meaningEn: God mercifully forgave the people of Nineveh.
pages.pictureHint: The same people and Jonah at peace in front of the quiet ancient city, soft warm dawn light in an empty sky. The king still clearly royal and apart. No figure, face, or hand in the sky. Calm and forgiven. No text.

refrain.meaningEn: A little one is brave when he trusts God.

pages.geez: ዳዊት ንእሽተይ ጓሳ ነበረ። ንኣባጊዕ ኣቦኡ የዕቅብ ነበረ።
pages.latin: Dawit n'ishtay gosa nebere. N-abagi' abu'u ye'qib nebere.
pages.meaningEn: David was a young shepherd. He watched his father's sheep.
pages.pictureHint: David, a Horn of Africa boy about twelve, deep warm brown skin, short black curly hair, no beard, kind dark eyes, plain undyed sand-linen knee-length tunic and a rope belt, bare feet, standing among three fat-tailed cream-and-tan highland sheep on a dry golden hillside. He watches the sheep. Empty soft sky. No lion, no bear, no army, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ኣንበሳ ወይ ድቢ ምስ መጸ፡ ዳዊት ንኣባጊዕ የድሕን ነበረ።
pages.latin: Anbesa wey dbi ms metse, Dawit n-abagi' yedhen nebere.
pages.meaningEn: When a lion or a bear came, David would save the sheep.
pages.pictureHint: The same David, staff in hand, standing in front of his fat-tailed sheep. A calm lion stands a few steps away and does not touch anyone. A bear waits farther up the hill, also calm, not attacking. No bite, no blood, no fear-monster faces. Deep brown skin, sand linen. Empty sky. No God, no text.

pages.geez: ኣቦኡ ንዳዊት መግቢ ሒዙ ናብ ኣሕዋቱ ኣብ ሰራዊት ሰደዶ።
pages.latin: Abu'u ni-Dawit megbi hizu nab ahwatu ab serawit sededo.
pages.meaningEn: His father sent David, carrying food, to his brothers in the army.
pages.pictureHint: An older Horn of Africa shepherd, deep brown skin, short beard, undyed sand linen, no crown, handing a cloth bundle of bread to the same young David. David holds the food. Far behind them, a few brothers in plain earth tunics stand by simple tents of an army camp. No king, no giant, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ኣብኡ ዓቢይ ጐልያድ ካብ ፍልስጥኤማውያን ንእስራኤል ጸውዐ።
pages.latin: Ab'u abiy Golyad kab flstimawyan ni-Isra'el tsew'e.
pages.meaningEn: There, big Goliath from the Philistines shouted at Israel.
pages.pictureHint: Goliath, a very tall Horn of Africa man, deep brown skin, short hair, short beard, dull bronze helmet and bronze scale armor, a long spear, mouth open as he shouts across a valley. He is big but his face is serious, not scary, not gory. Small soldiers in sand and sage linen listen from the far slope. No blood, no God, no text.

pages.geez: እቶም ሰራዊት እስራኤል ነቲ ጐልያድ ርእዮም ፈርሑ።
pages.latin: Itom serawit Isra'el neti Golyad r'iyom ferhu.
pages.meaningEn: The soldiers of Israel saw Goliath and were afraid.
pages.pictureHint: Three ordinary soldiers, Horn of Africa men, deep brown skin, sand and sage tunics, no armor crowns and no headscarves, faces clearly afraid as they look up at tall Goliath in dull bronze armor across the valley. No fighting, no blood, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ዳዊት ግና ንሳኦል እግዚኣብሄር ክሕግዘኒ እዩ በሎ።
pages.latin: Dawit gna ni-Sa'ol Igziabher khhgezni iyu belo.
pages.meaningEn: But David told Saul, "God will help me."
pages.pictureHint: The same young David, sand linen, no beard, speaking to King Saul. Saul is a grown man, deep brown skin, short beard, a simple thin bronze circlet, and a longer richer ochre-earth robe, clearly royal beside the boy. David's mouth is open. Empty soft sky, no figure in the sky. No armor on David yet, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ንጉስ ሳኦል ክዳኑ ኸደኖ። እቲ ክዳን ግና ዓቢይ ነበረ።
pages.latin: Ngus Sa'ol kdanu khedeno. Iti kdan gna abiy nebere.
pages.meaningEn: King Saul put his armor on him. But the armor was too big.
pages.pictureHint: King Saul, bronze circlet and richer ochre robe, setting a much-too-big dull bronze chest piece and helmet on the same small David. The armor hangs oversized on the boy; David's face, curly hair, and sand tunic still show. Saul looks kind, not angry. Camp tents behind. No blood, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ዳዊት ግና ወንጭፉን ሓሙሽተ ልሙፃት ኣእማንን ካብ ሩባ ወሰደ።
pages.latin: Dawit gna wenchfun hamushte lmutsat a'man kab ruba wesede.
pages.meaningEn: But David took his sling and five smooth stones from the stream.
pages.pictureHint: The same young David kneeling at a clear shallow highland stream, sand linen, no armor. In his hands a simple leather sling and exactly five smooth round stones from the water. More smooth stones in the stream bed. No giant, no sword, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ዳዊት ብወንጭፉ ናብ ጐልያድ ቀረበ። ኣይፈርሐን።
pages.latin: Dawit b-wenchfu nab Golyad qerebe. Ayferhan.
pages.meaningEn: David came up to Goliath with his sling. He was not afraid.
pages.pictureHint: The same small David, calm face, sand linen, leather sling in his hand, walking toward tall Goliath. Goliath stands in dull bronze armor with a spear, big but not monstrous, not wounded. A valley between them. David is not afraid. No stone thrown yet, no blood, no God, no text.

pages.geez: ዳዊት ሓንቲ እምኒ ወንጨፈ። ጐልያድ ኣብ ምድሪ ወደቐ።
pages.latin: Dawit hanti emni wenchefe. Golyad ab mdri wedeqe.
pages.meaningEn: David slung one stone. Goliath fell to the ground.
pages.pictureHint: The same David has just used his sling. One smooth stone rests on the ground. Tall Goliath in bronze armor has fallen and is sitting down on the earth, eyes closed as if asleep, no wound, no blood, no sword, no severed head. David stands calmly. Empty sky. No God, no text.

pages.geez: ሰብ እስራኤል ሓጎሱ። ዳዊት ብእግዚኣብሄር ሰዓረ።
pages.latin: Seb Isra'el hagosu. Dawit b-Igziabher se'are.
pages.meaningEn: The people of Israel rejoiced. David won with God's help.
pages.pictureHint: A small crowd of Horn of Africa people in plain sand and sage linen, smiling, hands raised in joy. The same young David stands in the middle, calm and glad, sand tunic, sling at his side. No giant, no body, no blood. Soft empty dawn sky. No figure, face, or hand in the sky. No text.

pages.geez: ንእሽተይ ዳዊት እግዚኣብሄር ምስ እመነ ብርቱዕ ኮነ።
pages.latin: N'ishtay Dawit Igziabher ms emene brtu' kone.
pages.meaningEn: When little David trusted God, he became brave.
pages.pictureHint: The same young David alone with two fat-tailed sheep on a quiet golden hill, sand linen, calm brave face, looking toward an empty soft sky. No giant, no army, no crown. No figure, face, hand, or light-being in the sky. Peaceful. No text.
